reason: E1 directly demonstrates that cryo-rolling and annealing of the same eutectic HEA system produces a refined hierarchical microstructure with simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement, supporting the core premises. However, the hypothesis adds mechanistic claims about reduced dislocation pile-ups and boundary stabilization that are not explicitly evidenced in the cited passages, and E2 provides only general background on eutectic alloys without specific support for the proposed mechanism.
premises: Cryo-rolling enhances stored energy in the ductile phase and limits recovery in the brittle phase.
Subsequent annealing induces selective recrystallization in the ductile phase and stabilizes phase boundaries.
This microstructural refinement reduces dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Reduced pile-ups mitigate local stress concentrations and microcracking.
The treatment simultaneously increases strength and ductility relative to the untreated state.
